strongest_angle: Norse cosmology structures the universe around the world-tree Yggdrasil and divides existence into nine realms as recorded in the 13th-century Poetic Edda and Prose Edda.

key_facts.fact: Norse mythology and its concepts of time, space, and cosmogony are primarily recorded from oral sources in the Poetic Edda, a collection of poems compiled in the 13th century.
The Prose Edda was authored by Snorri Sturluson and incorporates stanzas of eddic poems directly into its prose, serving as a primary structural source for Norse cosmology.
Norse cosmology divided the universe into nine realms, featuring Asgard as the realm of the Aesir and Alfheim as the realm of the Bright Elves around the world-tree Yggdrasil.
John Lindow's 2021 study on cosmogony and eschatology outlines the narrative sweep of Old Norse Mythology from the formation of the cosmos to the encounters between gods and giants.
